changes.note: A fifth data-style value, ornament: a centred diamond in --color-primary with hairline rules running out to both sides and fading toward the ends, drawn by CSS alone (no text content, no extra element). With a label part the label sits in the centre instead of the diamond. Horizontal only: a vertical separator with data-style="ornament" keeps its solid line. Forced colours reduce it to a system-colour rule with the diamond on it (both the hr and the label-less div form). The element, its role and its semantics are unchanged; the diamond is a pseudo-element with no content. No change for the existing styles.

Nested components keep their own parts. The stylesheet reached the label with descendant selectors, so a component nested inside with parts of the same name took this one's styles. The label is the root's child. Every part rule is now a child chain from the root, with the hops in :where(), so no rule changes specificity. No change for markup that follows the template.

data-size is now declared (it was in separator.css and in no manifest). It sizes a vertical separator only, and its default is empty because absence is a real value: an unsized vertical separator stretches to its flex line (height: 100%) instead of taking a fixed height. No CSS or behaviour change. 0.8-10's undeclared-attribute rule now makes this class of drift impossible: an attribute a component's CSS selects on that its manifest never declares fails the registry gate.

label.description: Optional text label centered on the separator

a11y.notes: The ornament style is decoration on a separator that is still a separator: an hr keeps its implicit separator role, a labelled div keeps role="separator", and the label is real text read as written. The diamond is a content-less pseudo-element, so there is nothing for assistive technology to announce. Use it for a break between sections, not as the only marker where a boundary matters: forced colors reduce it to a plain rule.
